# Feature: Sand tile — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #45 (Sand tile) from Terrain and Hazards before it is used in real levels. Effect: Leaves your footprints for you to follow back; no slowing. Unique: footprints only you read, left at no speed cost. Useful: retrace your route in sand, especially where you cannot see far. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** leaves your footprints for you to follow back; no slowing.

**So that** retrace your route in sand, especially where you cannot see far.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Sand tile for the first time in its teaching room (mech-45-sand-tile-room). Teaching moment: First room: a sandy room with two similar exits, one of which is a dead end. A player who does not notice their own footprints takes the same dead end twice and wastes the timer retracing it, which teaches that the prints are a record left for the player rather than decoration on the floor. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Walking on sand leaves clear footprints that persist for the rest of the attempt so you can see and retrace your own route
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: It does not slow you
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Enemies ignore sand prints
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Scent tracking is mud's job

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.
- No soft-lock: every reachable state has a legal move, a lose, or a reset.
- Definition audit: sand: floor variant defined here; it never slows the player (floor per mechanic 5 in this file)
- Definition audit: prints: visible record of the path walked, defined here for sand; prints in sand are readable only by the player, unlike mud per mechanic 47 in this file
- Definition audit: enemy: patroller or chaser per mechanics 31 and 32 in enemies-and-bots.yml; enemies ignore sand prints

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Sand tile's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Testing

Needs a mechanics playground: new — Test Level mech-45-sand-tile-room, built from this mechanic's teaching moment above. What to check there: every rule in Player-Facing Behavior, played in mech-45-sand-tile-room; the teaching moment's first (naive) action should fail as described and the corrected action should succeed. Record play sessions for replay: yes — sessions are the review evidence. Synergy rooms are explicitly deferred to a later run and are not part of this feature's check.
Named test cases (from the candidate file; all must be played):
- Test case prints persist and cost nothing: crossing sand leaves prints for the rest of the attempt and movement takes the normal one move per tile
- Test case adversarial dead-end retrace: entering the dead end and returning, the prints show the taken route and the untaken exit stays print-free
- Test case enemies ignore prints: blocked-by: 31 (patroller): an enemy crossing sand prints follows its own rule unchanged
- Test case restart and replay: restart clears every print, and a recorded session replays to the same end state
